title: Widening the stop took the win rate from 36% to 59% and made the strategy worse
author: person-person12
selftext:
The advice you get after a bad week is always the same, your stop is too tight, give it room. Its said with a lot of confidence and I have never once seen somebody put a number on it, so I measured it.

NQ, 5 minute candles, a 20 EMA reclaim entry, January 2020 to September 2026. One thing changed between runs, how far the stop sat from entry.

**1 ATR stop** 860 trades, 35.6% wins, profit factor 0.97
**2 ATR stop** 195 trades, 51.8% wins, profit factor 0.89
**3 ATR stop** 44 trades, 59.1% wins, profit factor 0.59

Every bit of extra room bought a better hit rate and a worse result, and all three lost money. The widest stop had the best win rate on the page and lost it the fastest.

The part I wasnt expecting was the trade count, 860 down to 44 on identical entry rules. As far as I can tell thats because a wide stop keeps you sitting in a position while the next several setups come and go without you, so **giving it room isnt only a decision about the loser, its a decision to skip most of your trades.**

Ran all three in [Agenticks](https://www.agenticks.ca/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=post&utm_campaign=autopilot&utm_content=ai_trading) with costs charged on both sides. None of these are strategies I would put money behind, I only wanted to know which direction the stop pushes the numbers before taking anyones word for it.

replies.author: person-person12
replies.body: yea it happens every time tbh. A wider stop gets hit less so the win rate climbs. The ones that do get hit are **way bigger** though, and they eat everything the extra wins brought in

replies.author: Repulsive-Worry5225
replies.body: yeah...finding the right parameters that isnt overfitting is devilishly hard

replies.author: person-person12
replies.body: yea and it gets worse the more settings you try, run a few thousand combos and one of them looks amazing on luck alone. Thats why I only moved the stop and kept three runs, it wasnt a search for the best number, it was checking the advice everyone gives. The wider stop **won more often** and the strategy still got worse every time

replies.author: Repulsive-Worry5225
replies.body: yeah thats what sucks. im also looking for more edges right now. felt like i was going too deep so now im stepping back, looking at basic stuff like momentum and mean reversion again

replies.author: person-person12
replies.body: Stepping back is the right call tbh. The test in this post was about as basic as it gets, one EMA and one stop rule, and it still taught me more than most of the **complicated setups** I've run, mostly because with that few moving parts you can actually see what broke. What market are you running the momentum stuff on?

replies.author: Repulsive-Worry5225
replies.body: trying it on MNQ, but you usung it on bitcoin honestly makes more sense. A Hurst exponent test showed MNQ is mean reverting anyway. maybe your strat works on individual stocks too?

replies.author: person-person12
replies.body: havent run it on single stocks yet tbh. The Hurst point is interesting tho, if MNQ keeps snapping back on the 5 minute then a wider stop gets rescued more often, which fits the **win rate climbing** as the stop moved out. It just didnt make the losers any cheaper when they did land

replies.author: Repulsive-Worry5225
replies.body: found a new edge, try running classifiers onto mnq
